packageRules.description: Only the lockfile moves for in-range updates: the ranges in the published packages' package.json are what consumers install against, so widening or raising one is a release decision made by hand with a changeset, not a Renovate update.

Peer ranges (react, react-router, next, nuxt, @angular/core, rxjs) say which framework versions each adapter supports. They change only in a deliberate release, once the adapter is tested against the new major.
The SDK's own packages link to each other through the workspace; changesets owns their versions.
Vite and Vitest move together: Vitest hoists its own Vite, and the docs app's @react-router/dev must use that same copy (CLAUDE.md, 'Vite 7, not 8'). One MR when either takes a new major.

zone.js is pre-1.0, so a 'minor' can break the Angular tests; take it with an Angular major, on approval. Its own group, because approval applies to a whole branch: inside the weekly minor/patch group it held that group back too.

Hold TypeScript below 7: 7.0 ships no programmatic API, which tsup's declaration build (and the app's typescript-eslint) needs. Remove once 7.1 is out and tsup supports it, matching skyscribe-app's rule.

CI runs on Node 22, the lowest version package.json's engines field supports, so the packages are tested where consumers' oldest supported runtime is. Raise the CI image, @types/node and engines together, in a release.
The renovate CI job's own image runs Renovate, which needs Node 24; keep it on the 24 line.
